headline: The M/M/infinity immigration--death flow has an exact Poisson invariant law, Charlier diagonalization, kernel formula, and trace-class positive-time semigroup atlas
nonclaims: a primitive periodic-orbit interpretation of the stochastic population process
any queue eigenvalue as a target zero, prime, Euler factor, root number or arithmetic local datum
a target functional equation, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya operator or Route-B construction
an unqualified statement about every infinite-state semigroup outside the positive-time Poisson theorem
external peer review, novelty certification or acceptance score

boundary_rows.law: pure death; delta_0 is the unique stationary law and all finite populations hit 0
pure birth with no stationary probability; population escapes to infinity
identity dynamics; every point mass is stationary
Poisson stationary laws collapse weakly to delta_0

boundary_rows.condition: mu down 0 with lambda fixed positive
boundary_rows.law: rho diverges and Poisson stationary laws are not tight
transition law converges in total variation to Poisson(lambda/mu)

route_a.strongest_failure: Population states and rates have no primitive arithmetic owner, logarithmic prime clock, target divisor, or Hilbert--Polya bridge.
route_a.strongest_positive: An intrinsic reversible Markov semigroup has a complete all-mode Charlier spectral and trace ledger.

theorem.boundaries: lambda=0 pure death, mu=0 pure birth, both zero identity, rho down 0 collapse, mu down 0 loss of tightness, and long-time Poisson convergence are separated faces.
theorem.gap: The L2(Poisson) spectral gap is mu; all nonconstant modes decay at integer multiples k mu.
theorem.kernel: P_t(n,m) is the convolution of Binomial(n,exp(-mu t)) survivors and Poisson(rho(1-exp(-mu t))) immigrants.
theorem.mixing: A shared-immigration coupling gives TV(P_t(n,.),P_t(m,.))<=min(1,exp(-mu t)|n-m|), and comparison to stationarity gives min(1,exp(-mu t)(n+rho)).
theorem.scope_boundary: The spectral product is source-local and is not identified with a target zeta, divisor, or arithmetic operator.
theorem.spectral: Charlier polynomials C_k(.;rho), normalized by sqrt(k!rho^k), satisfy P_t phi_k=exp(-k mu t) phi_k.
theorem.stationary: For lambda,mu>0 the unique reversible invariant law is pi_n=exp(-rho)rho^n/n!, rho=lambda/mu.
theorem.trace: For every t>0 the diagonal semigroup is trace class with trace (1-exp(-mu t))^{-1}; its source Fredholm product is product_{k>=0}(1-z exp(-k mu t)).
